assets.description: Bark: a HUD line icon of one peeled strip with its end rolled into a curl, shown beside bark in the backpack, on the "Add bark" button, and on the debarking bar. On the ground, a piece of bark is a peeled strip curved like the trunk it came off, dark outside and pale inside, with one end rolled into a tight curl, like the icon.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved adding a ground form, so bark can lie on the ground when taking down a building piece gives back more bark than the backpack holds. The HUD icon is unchanged.

assets.description: The foundation: four debarked logs laid side by side over one building-grid square, resting on two cross beams with a leg under each end. Each deck log differs a little in thickness, length, and turn, and the logs and beams show darker cut ends. The legs reach down to the ground, so they grow longer on the low side of a slope. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction lays the logs one per stage after the legs and beams go in.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The log wall: a 2 m stack of debarked logs laid along one edge of a foundation square. Each delivered log is cut in two, so each build stage lays two courses. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction lays the courses from the bottom up. A finished wall between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The door frame: two debarked-log posts on one edge of a foundation square, with a lintel across the top, 2 m tall. The doorway stays open. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction puts up the left post, the right post, then the lintel. A finished frame between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The cabin roof section: a sloped roof over one foundation square, resting on the tops of its walls. It slopes 12 degrees down to the front to shed rain, and sections one behind another share one continuous slope. Three faceted debarked-log rafters with pale cut ends rest on the front wall. Where a section has no section beside or behind it, debarked logs stacked on the wall, cut to the slope, fill the gap up to the bark. Four strips of bark, made like the lean-to's but pressed flatter, trimmed neater, and painted with a grain of streaks, cracks, and knots, lie over them like shingles from the front up, a little past the square's edges. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction puts up the rafters one per stage, then lays the bark one strip per stage. The roof above the player hides when they stand under it. Each section slopes down the way the player turned it. Its hip and valley corner pieces are the separate draft asset roof-corners.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The hip and valley corner pieces of the cabin roof. Where two roofs that slope at right angles meet, the corner section changes shape on its own: an outside corner becomes a hip, where two slopes meet at a ridge, and an inside corner becomes a valley, where they meet in a gutter. Each has a debarked-log rafter along each low edge and one corner to corner under the line where the slopes meet. Four rows of bark strips, made like the straight section's, are laid on both slopes from the eaves up, each cut along the meeting line and reaching a little past it, so on a hip each slope laps over the ridge and on a valley each slope tucks under the other. Logs cut to the slope fill any gap above a wall or a lower roof beside it. Construction stages match the straight section's.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The lean-to: two crooked front posts with forked tops, a ridge pole resting in the forks, and crooked stick rafters sloping to the ground at the back. Curled strips of bark, dark outside and pale inside with ragged lower edges, cover the rafters like shingles. The front is open. It is built in stages: each stick, then each strip of bark, fades in and is lowered into place.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

Each item has its own shape, a main colour, and an accent colour, such as a wooden handle on a steel blade. The item's name shows when the player points at its chip.

Also an icon for the debarked log, a build material that is not a backpack content. They share the backpack icons' style and renderer. Each build menu tile shows its structure's icon over its cost, drawn as material icons with counts.

assets.description: The chest: a rough box hewn from debarked logs, 0.9 m wide and 0.55 m deep. Its body has a square post at each corner, three stacked planks in each wall with thin gaps between them, and a wooden grip on each end. Its lid is three planks laid side by side with a small overhang, held by two battens across the top. Each plank is a slightly different shade, and cut ends show pale. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction builds the body in the first stage and puts on the lid in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The sawhorse: a pale beam of debarked log, 1.2 m long, resting 0.75 m up in the crook of two pairs of crossed legs, one pair near each end. The legs spread 0.6 m at the foot. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction stands up the legs in the first stage and lays the beam in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: A woodpile: two rails of debarked log on the ground, held in by two stakes at each end, with logs, debarked logs, and firewood stacked across them, four to a layer, from empty to full at five layers. Logs, debarked logs, and firewood use their approved shapes. Each layer rests in the gaps of the one below. As a blueprint, the rails and stakes show see-through.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved the stacked version: approved log, debarked log, and firewood shapes, layers nested in the gaps, debarked rails, and four stakes.

assets.description: How each kind of dropped thing looks on the ground, from one to many. A pile shows one copy of its kind for each thing it holds, up to 12. Firewood lies in a stack of 5, 4, then 3, each layer resting in the gaps of the one below. Bark lies in up to three rows of strips, each strip nested in the one below. Tools, food, the pot, and the bedroll spread around the middle. Firewood, bark, mushrooms, and the pot reuse their approved shapes. The axe has a steel head and a handle painted red at its end, the knife a bright blade, the drawknife a blue-steel blade with two wooden handles, and the fire striker is a flat steel loop. A handful of berries is seven red berries on a leaf. Dropped sticks never form a pile: they lie as normal sticks. The saw blade, the saw, and the plank are rough draft shapes added by the crafting feature.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The bedroll lying rolled up on the ground after the player drops it: the laid bedroll rolled up, green canvas outside with the red blanket spiralling through each end, a hemmed loose flap, and two leather straps with brass buckles.
